label: CASP Integrated Compliance Operating Model (MiCA + DORA + AMLR/TFR)
description: Treats MiCA, DORA and AMLR/TFR as ONE compliance programme for a Crypto-Asset Service Provider, not three. Maps where the frameworks overlap and where they diverge, designs a single operating model with shared controls, and hands off to the FCP gap-analysis and risk-assessment workflows for the AML/CFT legs.

modelTier.notes: Cross-framework article citations (MiCA 2023/1114, DORA 2022/2554, AMLR 2024/1624, TFR 2023/1113) must be accurate. Opus 4.8 strongly recommended for the overlap/divergence mapping.

claudeKnowledge.description: MiCA Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, AMLR (EU) 2024/1624, AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640, TFR (EU) 2023/1113, ESMA/EBA RTS-ITS, ESA DORA RTS, EBA Travel Rule and CASP risk-factor guidelines

guidedInputs.label: CASP Profile
guidedInputs.description: What kind of crypto-asset service provider is this operating model for? This drives which MiCA services, DORA criticality and AMLR exposures dominate.

options.label: Custodial exchange (trading platform + custody + fiat on/off-ramp)
Bank or credit/payment institution acting as CASP (Art. 60 notification)
Token issuer (EMT/ART) that also provides CASP services

guidedInputs.label: Home Member State (NCA)
guidedInputs.description: The EU member state of authorisation. Drives the lead NCA, national add-ons and FIU/Travel-Rule reporting conventions.

guidedInputs.label: MiCA Services in Scope (Art. 3(1)(16))
guidedInputs.description: Which authorised CASP services does the entity provide? Custody and operation of a trading platform raise both the DORA criticality and the AMLR monitoring burden the most.

guidedInputs.label: Primary Objective of This Engagement
guidedInputs.description: What decision is this operating model meant to support?

options.label: Design the integrated target operating model (greenfield / pre-authorisation)
Consolidate existing MiCA / DORA / AML silos into one programme
Produce the overlap/divergence map and shared-control catalogue only
Assess integrated programme for supervisory / internal-audit readiness
Harmonise incident, outsourcing and record-keeping across the three regimes

guidedInputs.label: Cross-Framework Domains to Prioritise
guidedInputs.description: Where the three regimes touch the same control. Leave blank to cover all six convergence domains plus the divergent ones.

options.label: AMLR CDD / UBO / monitoring + Travel Rule (distinct)

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues, Silos or Prior Findings
guidedInputs.description: Describe existing organisational silos, duplicated controls, prior NCA/audit feedback, or upcoming deadlines that the operating model must resolve.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. MiCA team and MLRO function report to different committees; DORA register of ICT third parties does not list the same custody sub-custodian named in the MiCA custody policy; Travel Rule solution went live but is not in the DORA critical-function inventory; two separate incident playbooks with different thresholds...

exampleInput: We are a custodial crypto exchange authorised as a CASP in Sweden (Finansinspektionen), ~140 staff, offering custody, an order-book trading platform, and EUR/SEK on- and off-ramps. We currently run three separate programmes with three separate owners: a MiCA authorisation/conduct team under the General Counsel, a DORA/ICT resilience team under the CISO, and an AML/CFT function under the MLRO — each with its own committee, its own outsourcing register, and its own incident playbook. The board has asked us to stop running them as three regimes and design a single integrated compliance operating model. Show me where MiCA (2023/1114), DORA (2022/2554) and AMLR/TFR (2024/1624 + 2023/1113) overlap so we can build shared controls, where they genuinely diverge so we don't over-collapse them, and a RACI for the consolidated model. Known pain points: our DORA register of ICT third parties does not reconcile with the sub-custodian named in the MiCA custody policy; our Travel Rule (TFR) solution is live but isn't classed as a critical ICT function under DORA; and we have two incident-reporting thresholds that conflict. Then tell me exactly which ANTON workflows to run next for the AML/CFT legs.

exampleValues.known_concerns: DORA ICT third-party register does not reconcile with the sub-custodian named in the MiCA custody policy. Travel Rule (TFR) solution is live but not classified as a critical/important ICT function under DORA. Two conflicting incident-reporting thresholds (one MiCA/market-abuse, one DORA major-incident). MiCA, DORA and AML each report into a different committee with no single accountable owner.
